idiom_name: dirty-row table + flush thread + sqlite3 batched transaction
implementation_notes: C provides no persistence context, so the classic structure is fully hand-written: a dirty table keyed by row id (one entry per key, so staging coalesces), a mutex that guards it, and a dedicated flush thread that waits on a condition variable, drains the table, and writes the batch in a single sqlite3 transaction using prepared statements (sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_bind/sqlite3_step). What replaces the classic structure: nothing - only statement batching and transactions are provided, not change tracking or deferral - and that is justified whenever per-change round trips dominate the workload. For low-volume writes, write straight through instead.
pitfalls: The queue lives only in process memory: a crash before a flush loses every staged change unless the buffer is logged first.
Forgetting to re-check the predicate around pthread_cond_wait (or signalling without the mutex) deadlocks or spins the flusher.
sqlite3 handles are serialized only when compiled thread-safe: confine the flush to one thread or enable SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 and expect lock contention.
